analysis.title: Fed pause ahead of expected ECB hold
key_insights: The FOMC held rates at 3.75%-4.00% in a ten-to-two vote and upgraded its growth assessment to "strong" from "solid". Chair Warsh cited stronger trend growth, record capital expenditure and low unemployment, and said it is the FOMC's responsibility to get inflation down.
Natixis economists say a December Fed rate hike now looks all but certain, barring a material shift in the economic data.

The FOMC will keep eight meetings a year. In 2027 one meeting will be devoted to monetary policy strategy with no vote or statement. In 2028 two meetings will focus on strategy and six on policy decisions.

European natural gas prices rose more than 4.5% to above €100/MWh, the first time since the 2022 energy crisis. Markets slightly raised their expectations for ECB hikes over the next year, though no hike is expected at the October meeting. Attention is on whether the Governing Council turns more hawkish.

The Bank of Canada raised its overnight rate to 2.5% from 2.25%, the first increase in more than three years, and will decide one meeting at a time. It said further hikes may be needed but it will proceed carefully.
The RBNZ surprised by leaving rates unchanged, and the NZD fell 1.1% against the USD and weakened against all G10 currencies.

Euro rates: the 2-year Schatz yield rose 4 bp to 3.13% and the curve flattened. The EUR swap 2s10s slope narrowed to 5 bp. The 10-year OAT-Bund spread tightened 2 bp to 154 bp and the BTP-Bund spread widened to 115 bp.
Credit: iTraxx Main tightened 0.5 bp and iTraxx Xover 4 bp, while CDX IG was stable. BASF tightened most (-5 bp) after its results. Bending Spoons issued €500M of 5-year debt (NC2) at 8.625%.

Alphabet's results disappointed. Revenue excluding partner payouts was $111.2bn (+27% YoY) against $111.3bn consensus. Google Cloud was $30.7bn vs $29.1bn expected with a $561bn backlog, but Search and Services fell short. FY-26 capex guidance is $195-205bn, in line with consensus. Shares fell 10% after hours.

Microsoft's Q1-27 revenue was $92.3bn vs $90.7bn consensus, Azure grew 48% YoY to $33.2bn and adjusted EPS was $4.89 vs $4.73 expected. Capex was $39.4bn vs $45.9bn forecast because third-party cloud capacity was delayed. Shares rose 2.8% after hours.

European bank Q3 results: BNP had a revenue-driven beat with strong trading and ~€19bn of OAT exposure. Santander was mixed with weaker revenue and a higher cost of risk. Deutsche Bank beat with revenue of €8.3bn and net income of €1.8bn. Standard Chartered beat and raised full-year guidance.
Stellantis' Q3 was weak, but North American AOI margin beat expectations. Industrial FCF missed at €-4bn. Shares rose 15% and 5-year CDS widened nearly 9 bp.
Airbus reported nine-month revenue of €50.6bn, adjusted EBIT of €4.5bn and net income of €3.6bn, and kept its FY2026 targets of 870 deliveries, €7.5bn adjusted EBIT and €4.5bn free cash flow.
US core PCE at 13:30 is the session's most important number, alongside Q3 GDP, personal income and spending. The ECB decision is at 14:15.
